Seminar Title:

Energy-Efficient Distributed Event-Region Estimation in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Minimum-Volume Ellipsoids.

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Prabeen Kumar Sahu ( Rollno : 517ec1010)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC 303(Seminar Hall), ECE Department

Date and Time:

13 Nov 2026 05.30PM

Contact:

Upendra Kumar Sahoo

Abstract:

Battery-powered Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely used for monitoring environmental
events, where identifying the spatial extent of an affected region is as important as
detecting the event itself. Conventional centralized approaches report the locations of individual
affected sensor nodes to a Fusion Center (FC), resulting in communication overhead that
increases with the number of affected nodes and causing excessive energy consumption near the
FC. This progress report presents a systematic development of a distributed framework for compact
event-region estimation using the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid (MVEE), referred
to as MVE in this report. The central idea is to replace the transmission of individual affectednode
positions with a compact geometric representation described by a constant number of
parameters.
The research progresses through three stages. The first stage establishes the feasibility of distributed
MVE estimation through local node cooperation, boundary-point extraction, core-set
reduction, and Khachiyan-based MVE computation. The second stage develops the Cooperation-
Then-Minimum-Volume-Ellipsoid Formation (CTMVEF) framework, introducing covarianceintersection-
based diffusion, boundary-node cooperation, adaptive weighting, and noise-aware
event detection. The boundary-node adaptive-weighted approach reduces communication energy
by approximately 71% compared with centralized reporting under the considered simulation setting.
The third stage extends the framework to practical bandwidth- and energy-constrained
networks through the Adaptive Event-Triggered Quantized Distributed MVE Estimation (AETQBCTMVEF)
framework. It incorporates quantization-aware fusion, adaptive bit-depth allocation,
innovation-based event-triggered transmission, and residual compensation, together with
a steady-state error bound that accounts for quantization, transmission staleness, and measurement
noise. The proposed approach achieves a reported joint savings factor of 7.92 while
maintaining competitive estimation accuracy. Overall, the work advances distributed eventregion
monitoring from basic geometric compression toward robust, communication-efficient,
and resource-aware estimation.
